clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with ethanol monitoring in the fermentation tanks, and which decision should real-time data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Identifies the real need and whether an in-line measurement is required at all before any product is specified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pain and decision unknown; the first step is a process diagnosis, not a purchase order.

clarification_questions.question: What ethanol concentration range must be measured, and is it expected at ppm or % level?
clarification_questions.why: The level determines whether Raman sensitivity is adequate and which detection limit is relevant.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Concentration level unknown; lab screening establishes whether it is ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: How clear or turbid is the wine during fermentation, and does it contain CO2 bubbles or solids?
clarification_questions.why: Turbidity, bubbles and particles affect the Raman signal and probe choice.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical state unknown; treated as a clear liquid pending lab screening on representative samples.

clarification_questions.question: What are the fermentation temperature, pressure and cleaning or sterilization regime, and how does the wine composition vary during the process?
clarification_questions.why: These conditions determine probe materials, cleaning compatibility and whether a calibration stays valid across the fermentation.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Process conditions unknown; a single-matrix calibration cannot be assumed valid over the whole fermentation.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the probe be installed in the tank, and how far is the analyzer from the measuring point; are any fibers already installed?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and existing fibers determine the fiber type and whether the analyzer can be located at the probe.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and distance unknown; no fiber length or fiber type is assumed.

clarification_questions.question: What reference lab method is used for ethanol today, and what accuracy does it achieve?
clarification_questions.why: A reference method is required to establish and validate any in-line accuracy claim.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method known; accuracy cannot be stated until a comparison design is agreed.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the measurement?
clarification_questions.why: These requirements define whether the proposed system is suitable and what can be specified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; no accuracy or response time is committed before the feasibility study.

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: S01 p.16 describes in-line Raman for glucose, acetate, lactate in bioprocess reactors (aqueous). The claim's statement that the materials show Raman 'for other fermentation metabolites in aqueous media' is a transfer of a bioprocess example to fermentation metabolites generally; the page does not mention ethanol or wine, and the claim's contrast with ethanol in wine is an inference the page does not support directly. Fix: State that the source shows in-line Raman for glucose, acetate and lactate in bioprocess cell culture, and that it does not address ethanol in wine.

different_context: The quoted sentence refers to NIR tracking glucose or glycerol in the millimolar range in a bioprocess monitoring context; the claim applies it to wine fermentation major components without saying so. Fix: Say the bioprocess example supports NIR for glucose or glycerol in cell culture, and that transfer to wine is an untested assumption.

overstated: The page says Raman is 'particularly well-suited for aqueous environments' in a bioprocess context; the claim presents this as settling the choice for wine, which the page does not show. Fix: Quote the aqueous-suitability statement as a bioprocess-context reason to test Raman on wine, not as proof for wine.

not_supported: S02 p.6 gives fiber transmission ranges, but it does not state that silica fibers carry the Raman range or the NIR range for this link; the link length is not given there. Fix: Report only that the silica fiber transmission range is 350-2400 nm (Vis-NIR) and that Raman suitability depends on the chosen fiber and laser, with link length unknown.

not_supported: The fiber coverage ratings (full/partial for NIR and Raman) are not stated on S02 p.6; the page only shows transmission ranges. The classification is an inference presented as a source fact. Fix: Present the fiber ranges as read from the chart and label the full/partial classification as the assistant's own interpretation to verify.

overstated: S01 p.11 says fluorescence can be superimposed on Raman for many organic compounds and can be eliminated with filters and probes; it does not show that fluorescence will dominate wine Raman spectra. Fix: Say fluorescence background may affect Raman spectra of wine and must be checked experimentally.

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

FLUO.nominal_range: UV/Vis excitation and emission; depends on the fluorescent species [S01 p.12]

UVVIS.nominal_range: UV 190-360 nm and visible; depends on target and setup [S01 p.5]

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
raman_fluorescence_background: Raman can be swamped by fluorescence background from many organic compounds; check signal quality first. [S01 p.11]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
